title: Flow
description: One end-to-end flow, written by people and agents in YAML under flows/*.flow.yaml; several flows may share a file as separate YAML documents. The envelope follows the Kubernetes Resource Model (apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec) as Backstage's catalog-info.yaml does; the steps follow Arazzo 1.0, naming a surface, a call or another flow of this repository instead of an OpenAPI operation. atlas reads this file and never writes it; what it observes goes into a FlowReport. Who writes what: 'author' fields need intent and are written by a person or an agent; 'from atlas' fields are ids copied from atlas output (atlas draft flows writes them); atlas checks both in its FlowReport.

name.description: from atlas (draft) or author. Unique across the repository's flows; Arazzo's workflowId.

title.description: author. What the customer or the system achieves through the flow. Required for Documented=True.

description.description: author. Anything a reader needs that the steps do not show.

labels.description: author. Identifying values to select flows by, such as domain or journey. Keys and values follow Kubernetes labels: an optional DNS-subdomain prefix (labels of at most 63 characters, 253 in all) and /, then a name of at most 63 characters.

annotations.description: author or atlas. Non-identifying values for tools and people; atlas sets flow-atlas.dev/location in reports.

sources.description: author. The decisions, documents and issues behind the flow, shaped as OKF 0.2 sources.

lifecycle.description: author. active: the code must bear the flow out. planned: steps may be missing. deprecated: not checked.

owner.description: author. The person or team who answers for the flow.

entry.description: from atlas when one component calls the first step, otherwise author. Where the flow starts outside the graph, such as a screen. The first step must be called by this component.

produces.description: author. Registry entries the flow issues, as registry:key.

step.description: A hop the flow must pass through; Arazzo's Step with surface, call, chain or flow in place of operationId, operationPath or workflowId. Hops between listed steps may be left out.

stepId.description: from atlas (draft) or author. Letters, digits, _ and -, as Arazzo 1.0 stepIds are.

surface.description: from atlas: a surface id from atlas query, trace or draft.

call.description: from atlas: a call id from atlas query or trace.

chain.description: from atlas: a chain id from atlas chains or draft flows. The step is the request and every surface it reaches.

flow.description: author: the name of another Flow used as one step.

role.description: author. What this component does in the flow, and what it leaves to others. Required for Documented=True on surface and call steps.

lifecycle.description: author. planned when the step is not built yet.
